one_month_reasoning: Jabil's own catalyst (Q4 FY26 print and FY27 guide, 2026-09-30) just passed: a beat ($4.40 core EPS, $10.6B revenue) and a $17.55 FY27 core EPS guide, but the stock fell 10% on the day (318.84 to 286.86) on back-end-loaded margins, a seasonal Q2 dip and capacity-ramp costs, then recovered half the loss to 304.41 in two sessions. No Jabil earnings fall in the window (Q1 FY27 is mid-December). What does fall inside: late-October hyperscaler Q3 calls (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta) with 2027 capex commentary, plus Celestica Q3 and Flex Q2 FY27 results in late October. Chain evidence (Celestica guiding 2027 growth above 65%, Quanta order visibility into 2027, Moody's/S&P capex into ~$1T in 2027) leans mildly supportive, but the July 2026 AI-infra drawdown shows these prints can cut either way and the group is high-beta. Post-earnings drift after a sell-the-news reaction to a beat is ambiguous. I therefore stay close to symmetric around spot at ~13.6% monthly vol (47%/3.46), median ~305, with very slightly fatter tails for the capex-print event risk.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28 core EPS ~$20.5 x 16x = $328) and FCF yield (FY28 FCF/share ~$18.4 at 5.5% = $334), weighted 60/40 and rounded to $328 for 12 months out.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (≈FY28, Sep-27 to Aug-28) $20.5 x 16x

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 $17.55 grown ~17%: revenue growth slowing from 24% to ~12-14% as AI base gets larger (Celestica and Quanta say 2027 demand visibility is strong; hyperscaler capex forecast to approach ~$1T in 2027), ~20-30 bps more core margin as the 4M sq ft ramp absorbs, and ~3-4% share count reduction from the $1.4B remaining buyback.

Peers on current prices: Flex $116.61 / FY27 adj EPS midpoint $4.58 = ~25x; Celestica $387 / 2026 EPS $11.30 = ~34x (low-20s on 2027). JBL trades at 17.3x its FY27 guide today; JBL historically carries a discount to these peers given lower margin (6.1% vs Celestica 8.2%, Flex 6.7%) and consumer/auto exposure. I apply 16x on a one-year-forward basis, a modest de-rating as growth decelerates from 34% to ~17%.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 adjusted FCF ~$1.8B / ~98M shares = $18.4/share at 5.5% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 $1.6B grown ~12% with earnings, capex held at 1.5-2% of revenue per management.
~104M now (106.9M FY26 weighted avg) less ~$1.4B remaining authorization plus further buybacks at ~$300-330.

Today's FY27 FCF yield is ~5.0% ($1.6B / ~$31.7B market cap); peers Flex and Celestica trade at lower FCF yields given higher multiples. 5.5% embeds a modest de-rating as AI growth matures and capex rises.

bear.story: AI capex digestion in 2027 (the July-2026 style scare becomes real: hyperscaler FCF goes negative, capex guides flatten), memory and component shortages stall rack shipments, the 4M sq ft buildout runs underutilized and FY28 core EPS lands ~$17 with the multiple compressing to ~11x, JBL's pre-AI EMS range.

base.story: Jabil delivers roughly the $44.5B / $17.55 FY27 guide; the late-September 2027 Q4 print guides FY28 core EPS ~$20-21; multiple settles ~16x as AI growth decelerates from 50%+ to the 20s.

bull.story: 2027 hyperscaler capex lands near the $1T-plus forecasts, Vera Rubin and ASIC rack ramps lift cloud/data center well above $17.5B, margins reach 6.5%, FY28 EPS ~$23 and the stock re-rates toward 20x, near Flex and Celestica.

thesis_break_reason: Around $205 the stock would be ~11-12x FY27 guided EPS and ~13% FCF-yield territory on guided FCF, i.e. the market would be saying the FY27 guide is materially wrong: an AI capex cut by a top-5 customer, loss of a major rack program to Celestica/Foxconn/ODM-direct, or margin collapse from the capacity ramp. That is below the 52-week low area of ~$190-245 reached before the AI guide was raised, and beyond ordinary 47%-vol noise relative to fundamentals.

reasoning: Basic facts: FY26 revenue $36.0B (+21%), core EPS $13.09, adjusted FCF $1.53B; FY27 guide $44.5B revenue, 6.1% core margin, $17.55 core EPS, ~$1.6B FCF; cloud/data center expected at $17.5B (+52%) and AI revenue +50%. The stock fell 10% on the print over back-end-loaded margins and ramp costs, then rebounded to $304 (17.3x FY27 guide). Industry lane read: the rest of the chain is consistently positive on 2027 volume. Celestica raised 2026 to $20.5B and expects 2027 growth to accelerate beyond 65%; Flex raised FY27 guidance (adj EPS $4.42-4.74, +39%); Foxconn/Quanta/Wiwynn report order visibility into 2027 with Vera Rubin and ASIC racks ramping; Moody's and others see hyperscaler capex nearing ~$1T in 2027; TrendForce sees 2027 server shipment growth above 2026's 17%; SEMI sees record equipment spend in 2027 (supports Jabil's capital-equipment +40%). Negatives from the chain: memory supply is the binding constraint and is being pulled away from diversified end markets, CoWoS capacity caps 2027 rack volume, and the July-2026 AI-infra drawdown (and Goldman cutting its JBL target from $482 to $375 in September) shows how sentiment-driven the group is. Peers trade at richer multiples (Flex ~25x, Celestica ~34x current-year), so JBL is not stretched relative to the group, but it is a lower-margin assembler and the whole group is off its highs. Valuation blend gives ~$328, about 8% above spot. Scenarios (190/330/470 at 25/50/25) give a mean ~$330. I map that to a lognormal with median ~$322 and sigma ~0.42 (slightly below the 47% realized vol because some of that vol was the AI-sentiment whipsaw, but with a hand-fattened left tail for capex-digestion risk). The result: P(>=304) ~0.555, P(>=411) ~0.28, P(>=213) ~0.83. Research limited to web search/fetch and Twelve Data quotes; the analyst-target endpoint was paywalled.
